ops.title: Which cc-transcript Python modules are native-backed facades vs stay Python (current as of v14.6.1 — the ASYNC persistence tier), the actor/binding recipe, and the fleet migration state

ops.body:
The native-facade conversion pattern: Python COMPUTATION dies, compute runs in the `_native` core, Python keeps only the public typed surface, rehydrating what the core computes. **As of v14.5.0 (14.6.1 current) the persistence + tailing tier is natively ASYNC**, reversing 14.2's sync ruling.

**The async engine shape:** one generic std-only `Actor<E>` in core (`rust/crates/core/src/actor.rs` — mpsc + thread, jobs are closures, total delivery: every future resolves through failed opens/drain/close); the py bridge (`rust/crates/py/src/actor_bridge.rs`) returns asyncio Futures resolved via call_soon_threadsafe (aiosqlite's mechanism in Rust). SQL runs GIL-FREE on the actor (op outside `Python::attach` — a review-caught critical); delivery failures are swallowed wholesale (a panic would strand the actor); params convert on the calling thread (OverflowError/ProgrammingError stay synchronous); open-time errors arrive via `await open()`. The cross-thread affinity check is gone. Idiom family everywhere: `x = await X.open(...)`, `async with x:`, `async with store.transaction()` (raise-on-conflict kept, owner check-and-set under a threading.Lock, begin/commit/rollback inside try/finally with tolerant rollback). `judge.run_verdicts` serializes persist on a dedicated lock (14.6.1 — concurrent persists raced the exclusive transaction). The ledger tier (decisions/heartbeats) is a stdlib-only `ConnectionActor` in ledger.py (Go co-writer DDL bytes untouched; `_serve` guards closed-loop delivery). Watcher: async `tick()` + `stream(interval)`.

**Still Python/sync, each for a named reason:** disktruth (Go subprocess protocol), evidence.harvest/run_git (serial git subprocess; only record_harvest is async), and in captain-hook the hook HANDLERS (sync plugin contract — the "Option A" boundary: sync dispatch skeleton, leaf asyncio.run bridges holding per-process cached ledger handles). The "judge eval math + sampling stay Python for CPython Random reproducibility" carve-out DIED 2026-07-20 (post-14.6.1 stack 7fbe7c6..f2dddbd): sample_windows, sample_audit, exact_upper_bound, and similar.py's ranking are native, re-seeded on core `rng.rs` (splitmix64 over sha-256 of decimal-string seed material — seeds cross the FFI as str(seed), so arbitrary ints work); draws changed once, declared BREAKING in the changelog. AGENTS.md § Ownership now binds NEW domains ("Rust-first from birth", "Python keeps exactly four shapes") and the repo-local `rust_owns_semantics` llm gate fires on cc_transcript Python edits that introduce computing functions without _native.

**Fleet state (all shipped, CI green):** cc-steer main bc1d307 — composition over STEER_SCHEMA, v13→v14 non-store APIs migrated (parser.stream/discovery fns/SessionActivity/turn_ref_from), scrub moved to the dict layer + truncate-safe scrub_text on previews, pin >=14.6.1,<15. captain-hook main 139f65d7 — async end-to-end review subsystem, ReviewStore composition, daemon writer on one persistent loop, reconciled onto upstream's own 14.4-sync migration (10.5.0) with feature grafts, pin [judge]>=14.6.1,<15.

**Traps burned in this release:** ty is a local NO-OP in cc-transcript/cc-steer (see [[ty-config-poisons-local-checks]]); parallel sessions race version tags (14.3/14.4/14.6.0 were all taken mid-flight — the async release renumbered twice, landing as 14.5.0+14.6.1 with the sdist job's version guard the enforcing gate); rebases across concurrent same-file migrations produce SILENT semantic merges (a dropped import, dropped awaits, a concatenated unsatisfiable pin) — always full-suite re-gate post-rebase and gate the push on the verdict in a separate command; pipe-tail `$?` masks exit codes. Parity batteries `_native.activity_lift`/`query_session` stay unwired/undeleted. See [[cc-family-v8-release-mechanics]], [[never-build-docs-locally]].
